How to read this tab
panels.markdownContent:
**Live engine rates beside the benchmarked figures.** Every live line is a ratio of counter rates over 5 minutes, so it is reset-aware and does not depend on how many requests there were. The engine updates these counters **when a request finishes**, so a long reply shows up at its end, and a line has gaps while nothing finishes.

- *Decode tok/s a stream* = generated tokens / decode seconds. It is a **per-stream** rate: with N streams decoding together the pair's total is about N times this (the *all streams* panel shows the total by wall clock).
- *ms a round* = decode seconds / (rounds − requests); *tokens a round* = generated / rounds; *accepted / drafted* = draft tokens kept / draft tokens verified.
- *Prefill tok/s* = (prompt − cached) tokens / prompt-pass seconds. TTFT also holds queueing, restore and the first round.

**Reference lines** (legend entries starting `bench:`) come from the recipe's records: the sampled probe `runs/overnight-20261122/k265/ctl1.probe.json` and `k269` (thinking off, short prompts, 1 / 2 / 4 streams), `runs/k278` (cold prefill 32K / 96K, greedy decode at 300K) and `runs/cache-20261122` (8K turns). The 4- and 8-stream totals marked *dec4* / *dec8* are the decode cells of `runs/suite-fused-20261121` and `suite-fused-next2-20261121`. The sampled probe stops at 4 streams and uses short prompts; live traffic runs up to 8 streams on contexts of tens to hundreds of thousands of tokens, so a gap to a reference line is a difference in workload first. Compare *ms a round* and *prefill tok/s* before reading a tok/s gap as a regression. Details: `runs/observe-review-20261123/RESULTS.md`.

panels.title: About this tab
panels.markdownContent: The engine publishes some families twice: once under its own name and once under vLLM's, so vLLM dashboards work unchanged. These panels show the vLLM-named copies; the values equal the native series shown on the other tabs.

panels.title: About this tab
panels.markdownContent: The collector on each Spark scrapes `localhost:8000/metrics` every 30 s. Only rank 0 (the head, `gx10-eb0e`) serves that endpoint, so the worker's target reads **up = 0** all the time and every `tensorfold:*` series comes from the head; the head reports both ranks where a family has a `rank` label (spill tier, KV shard). A drop of the head's `up` to 0 is the engine restarting or stopped.

About this tab
panels.markdownContent: Pick any engine series in **Series** at the top: all 200 `tensorfold:*` series that hold samples are listed, then the 90 retired `tensorfold_*` / `tensorfold_health:*` names (they stopped on 2026-11-10 and 2026-10-31: widen the time range to see them). The left panel shows the samples as stored, one line a label set; the right one the per-second rate, which is the reading that makes sense for a counter.
